key_insight: Boosting noisy quantum classifiers can achieve the same classification-accuracy target with fewer circuit executions than probabilistic error cancellation, without reconstructing ideal quantum outputs.
engineering_relevance: For supervised quantum learning, task-aware ensembles offer a potential way to reduce sampling costs as circuit depth and physical noise increase.
method: Combine noisy parameterized quantum circuits using AdaBoostR and Real AdaBoost.
Compare boosting with probabilistic error cancellation at a matched learning target.
Establish a shared classification-risk bound from empirical margin loss for specified architectures under Pauli noise.
evidence_signal: Finite-shot teacher–student simulations across circuit depths and noise strengths showed lower execution costs at matched accuracy and higher test accuracy than the corresponding reference.
watch_item: The advantage is task-dependent and demonstrated for specified architectures and simulated noise; performance on hardware and broader datasets remains to be established.
paper_title: Beyond Error Mitigation: Using Boosting for Noisy Quantum Machine Learning
